div.span: Because Jesus left no written texts, the claim of his divinity depends entirely on the accuracy of the Gospel accounts. If the Gospels are assumed to be fully accurate, then error could only originate from Jesus himself - either by deliberately deceiving his followers in being authorized by God, by sincerely speaking under delusion, or by being influenced by an unseen/demonic source (knowingly or unknowingly).

div.b: How strongly does the claim resist fabrication and error?

div.span: To be able to distinguish between truth and falsehood, there must be some identifiable property between competing claims that would render one true and the other false.

span.b: What is the epistemological difference between an honest man and a liar?

div.span: People lie to gain something (ex. money, status, revenge) they can't get by being honest. But lies fundamentally contradict reality, and so any attempt to mix truth with lies inevitably snowballs and exposes those contradictions over time into unresolvable inconsistencies.

span.b: ifference between divine inspiration and demonic inspiration?

div.span: God, angels, and demons all act in mysterious ways, making it initially appear impossible to distinguish between them.

Both are beyond our capacity to sensually witness and verify, yet if God is fundamentally True while demons preach falsehood, then a demonic influence will appeal to arguments that inhibit proper reasoning, thus
disabling one's ability to distinguish truth from falsehood.

font.b: Stong by character assessment, weak by logical consistency - which is resolved by faithful historical and textual preservation

span.span: - Jesus gained little besides attention - both positive and negative. However, he is depicted as trying to conceal aspects of his identity (the “Messianic Secret”), meaning he intentionally wanted to suppress that same attention he was getting. As such, when paired with his apparent alignment with selfless moral values, the label of "liar" doesn't best fit him.

span.style: color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent;

span.font: However, the claim of Jesus' divinity culminates in the Hypostatic Union (3 Persons, 1 God), where we've already established that there is no coherent, identifiable distinction between the Persons. This renders the doctrine epistemologically indistinguishable from a false or fabricated claim

font.span: - unless its textual authority is proven perfect and superior to all alternatives
(as the True religion of the True God is expected to be the epitome of epistemological truth, with all other false alternatives necessarily contradicting reality in some way)
. Thus, its certainty must be anchored in the New Testament's preservation

span.span: - If Jesus were mentally unstable or delusional, his debates with highly educated legal scholars would have exposed him. In public debate, intelligence or incompetence becomes clear; Jesus' ability to challenge experts in Jewish law indicates clarity and intellect, not insanity. Otherwise, more intelligent opponents would have surely taken advantage of his mental weakness to elevate themselves, especially since the interpretation of Jewish law requires specialized education.

font.span: - Jesus performed miracles that could only have been authorized by God - such as the true revival of the dead - something demons cannot do (they can only make us think they can).

- A demonic influence will also not proactively encourage people to "know [truth] by [its] fruits", which Jesus taught. It's not in their interest to empower one's journey towards truth and to learn how to distinguish it from falsehood - they thrive on
ignorance

div.span: - Muhammad gained power, fame, and women, yet this only occurred after 13 years of unwavering commitment to his message - against offers of power, kingship, bribery, women, public humiliation, severe persecution, attempts on his life, and even when the revealed message was against his own interests. As such, the claim that Prophet was a liar who just wanted attention doesn't best fit the data.

div.b: What possibilities are there for fabrication and error with the claim's custodianship?

font.b: Bad faith, revisionism, and gradual Christological development

div.span: If any significant fabrication or error occurred, then mainstream Christianity would fundamentally differ from Jesus' original message. Evaluating custodianship therefore requires exposing the link between the historical Jesus and the earliest form of mainstream Christianity. Since Paul's letters are the earliest surviving Christian writings, and his theology later became mainstream, the question reduces to whether Paul's message corresponds to Jesus' original ministry. This exposes the following potential sources of fabrication and error:

span.b: Jesus and Competing Claims' Textual Silence

font.span: Jesus didn't write any texts himself. Meanwhile, the writings of rival early Christian groups are entirely lost. It is therefore possible that competing portrayals aligned more closely with the historical Jesus - without us ever knowing with certainty.

Paul never met the earthly Jesus and began preaching 1–6 years after the crucifixion. His letters were sent to communities 400–900 miles away (Rome even farther), and he claims that, 3 years after his conversion, his message was verified in a 15-day private meeting with Peter and James only in Jerusalem (Galatians 1:16-19).
If this authorization was private and self-attested, the strength of his claims rests entirely on Paul's personal trustworthiness, leaving room for undetectable error or bad faith.
Because his audiences lived far from Jerusalem, verification could take weeks or months, delaying correction and widening the window for doctrinal divergence during a time of competing claims.

Knowledge of Jesus' ministry comes primarily from the Gospels, which were written after Paul's preaching and rely on unknown transmitters and now-lost sources. It is therefore possible some (or all) were written to corroborate Paul's theology.
Earlier Gospel traditions appear to reflect a lower Christology
(ex. Mark doesn't even mention the virgin birth),
while later traditions exhibit a higher Christology
(ex. John presents Jesus as pre-existent and divine)
. As such, the it becomes possible that the Gospels correspond with a rising, new interpretation of Jesus' message.
- Looking at the Gospels' earliest preserved manuscripts (in the 2nd

and 3rd centuries), they contain a minority of variants that significantly affect the Christology of the affected passage. This raises the possibility that earlier copies may have had a different Christological rating than the ones we have now.

div.span: - Ignoring the synoptic chains' reliance on unknown transmission and lost works, what is known from Q/Logia also reflects a lower Christology than later works. This makes it possible that earlier Christianities believed in a lower Christology than later ones.

font.span: Notes: the books of Acts, 2 Peter, and Jude are omitted here as they are not fundamental to these points.

Acts actually states that Paul immediately went to Jerusalem and was verified openly, which opens a discussion on whether the two accounts contradict (or if the account in Acts was actually referring to his second visit rather than his first, considering the similarities).

Regardless, while Acts does give more information on Paul's first visit in Jerusalem, it was written after Paul's own letters were written (10-40 years later), and if it was authored by Luke, then he didn't meet the earthly Jesus either. Moreover, while 2 Peter attests to Paul's writings as scripture, it was written close to the time of Paul's death (15-20 years later) and shares over 70% of content with the book of Jude (and it is unknown which book took from what). As such, none of these
address the fundamental claim that Paul's theology differed from Jesus' message, and they could themselves also have been written revisionally.

div.span: If any significant error or fabrication occurred, then the mainstream Quran will fundamentally differ from Muhammad's original teaching. Evaluating custodianship therefore requires exposing the link between Muhammad's recitation and the earliest Quranic text.

Since the earliest manuscripts date to his lifetime, the question reduces to whether the text Muslims preserved corresponds to what Muhammad recited. This exposes the following potential sources of fabrication and error:

b.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;
font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: Muhammad was illiterate and so he didn't write any texts himself. While there were no competing claims to how the Quran was transmitted, i
t is possible (in principle) that what was preserved could have diverged from what he recited.

- Muhammad's illiteracy, lack of poetic skill, and lack of time in his day makes it difficult to identify him as the author of the Quran, which was an entirely unique genre of literature and with a power that caused the geographical elimination of deeply ingrained polytheism and tribalism. As such, it opens the possibility that someone else authored the Quran, or perhaps a committee of authors.
- The Quran has many instances of incorrect grammar, which could have also been a result of Muhammad's own illiteracy.

span.style: color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); background-color: transparent; font-size: 8px;

div.span: The Quran was revealed chronologically over a period of 23 years, yet the modern Quran does not place the verses in chronological order. This raises the possibility that the order was changed to cover up some issue that would be exposed if analyzed in chronological order.

span.style: color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent;
color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent;

div.span: The Quranic verses were often revealed in immediate response to unpredictable circumstances, to which they were immediately memorized by those who witnessed it. Given that there was no

span.span: revision, proofreading, correction, or alteration to the original words, this raises a significant possibility that the Quranic message is logically self-contradictory on a fundamental level

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: The Quran was only formally compiled into a single, complete, written book after the Prophet's death.

span.style: background-color: transparent; font-size: 8px; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: Considering that efforts involved the gathering of scattered materials (like writings on palm trees and rocks) and cross referencing them with hundreds of individuals who memorized the text, it raises the possibility of
missing fragments, misordering, or gaps in witness testimony.

span.style: font-size: 2px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); text-align: center;
background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: - After the Quran started to spread internationally (to non-Arab speakers) 20 years after the Prophet's death, diacritical variations among accepted recitations were causing disputes. As a result,

Uthman commissioned a single, diacritically standardized version of the Quranic text, and ordered all other existing written codices to be burned. This opens the possibility that legitimate codices or readings could have been eliminated.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: The Quran was revealed in specific historical contexts that are essential for its interpretation, and the primary historical records of those contents were compiled 100-250 years after the Prophet's death.

This long gap in the transmission of the contextual material creates a significant window for error, misunderstanding, or even deliberate fabrication of events to support later theological or political agendas.

span.style: font-size: 2px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); text-align: center;

div.span: Notes: even though the "contextual reinterpretation" section is more about how the Quran is understood rather than whether or not the Quran's text was preserved properly, it is included here for completeness: those who witnessed the Quran's revelation were also the witnesses of its context. The "verse of stoning" (an alleged verse that was memorized during Muhammad's life but not preserved in the Quran after he died) is omitted here, as it the only instance of such an event occurring, was heavily debated and its custodianship is far weaker than the Quran's, and falls under the greater topic of verse abrogation.
